solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman's greeting abrupt, extremely surly

parts.note: abrupt means curt

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word surly

explanation.surface: A woman greets someone in a short, sullen way.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is the bob of the knees traditionally made by a woman as a respectful salutation.

clue.text: About time for puss

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A question of when it is time to feed the puss.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is an affectionate everyday name for a domestic feline.

clue.text: Intention to participate in regular payment for clothing

indicators.note: to participate in something is to be within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: rent is a payment made regularly for a home
an intention is an aim

explanation.surface: Someone means to join a scheme of instalments to pay for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Southern cleric, misfit, altered reflective judgement?

indicators.note: altered says the letters of cleric and misfit are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A misfit clergyman from the South, changed in his ways, looks back on himself critically.
explanation.definitionFit: Judging oneself while reflecting on one's own faults is critical self-examination; the question mark marks the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Relative from America in the money?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: coin is money, as in 'coining it'
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A wealthy family member who comes from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a kinsman, the child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Oil tax — one part adjustable — take it or leave it

indicators.note: adjustable says the letters of oil, tax, one and part can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax on oil, one part of which can be changed, offered on a take-it-or-leave-it basis.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on that a buyer may choose or decline, such as a car accessory, is not compulsory.

clue.text: Saucy dance?

parts.note: a Latin dance that shares its name with a spicy sauce, so it is a 'saucy' dance in a punning sense

explanation.surface: A cheeky, risqué piece of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like it means cheeky; here it means sauce-like, since the dance is named the same as a Mexican sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin American ballroom style shares its name with a tomato and chilli condiment.

clue.text: Military facility shuts, nine redeployed

indicators.note: redeployed, as troops are moved around, says the letters of shuts and nine are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army base closes and nine soldiers are posted elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated corrugated-iron shelter, widely used by the British military in both world wars.

clue.text: Test trouble

definitions.meaning: a test or experiment, as in a drug study

explanation.surface: Something that tests you causes you difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an experimental check and an affliction that tests one's patience.

clue.text: Packages gripping non-drinker in Waterloo, Stamford Bridge, say?

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bales are bundled packages, as of hay or cotton
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: Parcels being carried by a teetotaller at two London places: a station and a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is a London station and Stamford Bridge is Chelsea FC's stadium, but both are also historic fights: Waterloo in 1815 and Stamford Bridge in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo and Stamford Bridge are both famous military engagements, given here as examples, hence 'say?'.

clue.text: Black vessel in stream

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: A dark pot lying in a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word, not an insertion signal. A burn is the Scottish word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a small brook is called a burn.

clue.text: Beer from Wales

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the word Wales, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A beer brewed in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer, often a traditionally brewed one.

clue.text: Camp sorry to change military formation

indicators.note: to change says the letters of camp and sorry are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A sorry encampment needs to reform into a new unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A large army unit made up of two or more divisions is a corps of the land forces.

clue.text: Excitedly to race pro associated with group

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitated movement, so the letters of to, race and pro are jumbled

explanation.surface: A professional rushes eagerly off to compete with a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate means relating to a company or a body of people acting together.

clue.text: Describing system of measurement, writer with short ruse?

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as me

indicators.note: short means a word cut off at the end, losing its final letter

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A writer pulls a small deception while describing a measuring scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter, K, from TRICK, leaving TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Metric describes the decimal system of metres and kilograms.

clue.text: Ridicule about six as extravagant

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to lash someone is to criticise or scorn them severely
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Mocking around six o'clock seen as over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means extravagant, profuse or generous to excess.

clue.text: Popular picture, perhaps, still being sold

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a print is a picture, for example a reproduced photograph

explanation.surface: A well-liked picture remains on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is in print is still available from the publisher for purchase.

clue.text: Singular label for men only

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A unique label marking something males-only.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is an event for males alone.

clue.text: Working group arrive with German note secured

indicators.note: secured means held fast inside, so the second part is enclosed

parts.note: to arrive is to come
mit is the German word for with
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A working party turns up alongside a German, with a written message safely in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with German' is a single piece: the German for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee is a body of people appointed to work on a particular task.

clue.text: Less important part of farm in Oregon

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smaller section of a farm in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means lesser or of lower significance.

clue.text: Mine dump recalled

indicators.note: recalled, as if called back, says the word for dump is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

explanation.surface: A slag heap at a mine is remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a colliery dug into the ground for coal is commonly called by this short word in Britain.

clue.text: Phoned about family position

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rang means phoned
kin means family

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned to ask about the family's social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a place or standing in a graded order, as in a league table.

clue.text: Blunder with English? Nonsense

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or error

explanation.surface: An English mistake dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, literally stomach lining, is a colloquial word for worthless talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Make mistake — Deirdre oddly ignored

indicators.note: oddly ignored says the odd-numbered letters of Deirdre are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Deirdre slips up, and her quirks are overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong or blunder.

clue.text: Senior common room is most profligate first of all — economise

parts.note: SCR is the abbreviation for a senior common room, the staff lounge at a British college

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of each of the words is, most and profligate

explanation.surface: The college staff lounge, the most wasteful of all, must cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be thrifty and save money, as in 'scrimp and save'.

clue.text: Exchange involving pub worker, no end

indicators.note: no means without, so the word end is taken away

parts.note: a bartender works behind the bar of a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swap involving someone serving drinks that never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' looks like 'endlessly', but it removes the letters E-N-D from the middle of the barman's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To barter is to trade goods for other goods without money.
